analyst_view.overall: This Madeira derby, the first top-flight meeting in five years, sets 15th against 13th. Mitchell van der Gaag's Marítimo have 8 points from 10 games and have not won in the league since 16 August, and Record (25 November) expects four changes, with left-back Paulo Henrique back from his knock and Fran Veites in goal. Nacional have 10 points from 11 and two 1-0 wins in their last three under João Henriques; each of their last four games had exactly one goal. Nacional are without Ulisses, Filipe Soares and Léo Santos, Wesley Gasolina is unlikely and Liziero close to a return, and the numbers already cut Nacional's goals for these. The Barreiros is close to sold out, the numbers do not treat the game as a derby, and Miguel Fonseca (Porto FA) was named referee on 25 November; his record is not yet in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals and already take Gasolina, Liziero and Léo Santos off Nacional's goals (about -22% between them). Yesterday Marítimo's defensive doubts held me at the numbers, but Paulo Henrique is now expected back at left-back, which leaves the points that pull down: Marítimo's weak scoring (9 in 10), Nacional's run of one-goal games and a tense, full-house derby between two sides near the bottom. I lean a little lower, to about 2.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.4 corners and already add a little for Marítimo's recent corner count (+2.6%) and take a little off Nacional's (-2.0%). Marítimo at home in front of a full house should push forward, but Nacional's absentees are mostly not wide players and nothing I found clearly moves corners, so I stay at 8.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. They already take 7.8% off because Nacional have been booked less than usual lately, and they do not treat this game as a derby. It is the Madeira derby, both clubs are near the relegation zone and the Barreiros is close to sold out, so I lean higher by 10%, to about 4.8. Miguel Fonseca was named referee; the numbers have not used his record yet, and this lean does not rest on him.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.5 shots and already cut Nacional's side by 7.8% for their low recent shot count. Marítimo should have more of the ball at home, while Nacional under Henriques won 1-0 twice and may sit deeper; these pull in both directions. Marítimo had six days' rest after 120 minutes in the cup, which is enough, so I stay at 25.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target and already add 4.2% to Marítimo because Nacional have conceded plenty on target lately. Marítimo's finishing has been poor and Nacional are missing some attacking options, but the numbers' ratings and missing list already reflect both, and I have put the tight-derby point on goals, so I stay at 9.7.
